what: Known section-detection defects of the parser as of the 150-filing blast-radius sample (docs/milestones/M02-blast-radius.json): filings that miss a required item (1, 1A, 7, 7A, 8). `fixed` lists the two cases the parser was changed for; tests/unit/parsing/test_known_defects.py keeps them fixed. Every item in `cases` is `needs_gold_label`: nobody has shown where it starts, so none is asserted. To assert one, add it to expected_found with its evidence and a strict-xfail test.
source: docs/milestones/M02-blast-radius.json (python -m eval.blast_radius, seed 20261118); the before-fix measurement is docs/milestones/M02-blast-radius-before-fix.json
how_to_run: the filings are cached by `python -m eval.blast_radius` under data/fixture_candidates/blast/; the tests skip when a filing is not cached

fixed.was: Item 1 missed: the heading is fused with the section's first sentence ('Part I Item 1. Business The Allstate Corporation was incorporated ...'), too long to be a heading
fixed.fix: pipelines/parsing/sections.py: a known item title followed by a new sentence is a fused heading; the sentence becomes the section's first text

fixed.was: Item 7A displaced: 'ITEM 8,' (the first fragment of a cross-reference inside Item 7) was taken as the Item 8 heading and, sitting before the real Item 7A, won the section order
fixed.fix: pipelines/parsing/sections.py: 'ITEM N,' with no title is a cross-reference fragment, not a heading (a title that wraps and ends in a comma is still a heading)
